After hearing a bit about Spooky's House of Jumpscares after it first came out, I had a few expectations for it, but tried to limit what I read until I got around to actually getting it. It's free on steam, but I only just now got around to actually downloading it. I played until 150 rooms last night, and of the thousand rooms, maybe that's not enough to really form an overall idea about the game, but I had some thoughts about it I think might help you decide whether or not you should even bother with the game, free or not.

First of all, I'll make this as spoiler free as possible, but anything after the dashes below is going to probably ruin if for you. Before that, let me give a few things that I can to inform you whether or not this game if for you without any spoilers. There's not much, but I can say:

  1. If you tend to get bored easily, don't play this game.

  2. The graphics are consistent.

  3. There is both humor and horror along with the cuteness.

  4. It's not random chance-- it was designed the way it was for a reason.

And that's about it for things that I can think of that are both helpful in forming a decision, and spolier free.

Sound

I want to say, before anything else, Spooky's is an excellent example of the mood of the game being very dependent on the background music. Sound design isn't normally the most talked about thing in a game, but for Spooky's, the sound design is half the horror. Relying on the music was a good choice, because where the graphics have to stay a certain level of cutesy, it can do the job of progressively making the mood more tense. The sound track is dark, and changes for different situations. There was a point at which I read in a note "I can hear it's clicking," and after putting the note down, the music changed, giving the described clicking noise. I never even saw what was supposed to be chasing me, but the music alone prompted me to get the hell out of there. The music isn't really exceptional itself, but it is used in such an effective way, which in other settings might have come across as cheesy, I have to give it props. It is played off the cute graphics well. All other sounds are hardly worth mentioning. So far, they've been standard. They're not glaringly bad, but also not extraordinary in any way.

Gameplay

Well, what can I say? You press forward most the time. Press forward, open door. Press forward, open door. Press forward, read note, open door. The manual the game presents to you in the beginning mentions "use weapon," but for at least 150 rooms, there is no weapons. If you get bored easily, don't play this game. I walked forward and opened doors for 30 minutes, and only saw one enemy that could harm me, although, there might have been another I just noped away from too fast.

The jumpscares wear off very quickly. There are cardboard cut outs that pop out regularly, but they stopped being scary at the third one for me. I haven't run into much more than the one enemy (and one possible enemy/well placed music that made me freak out and run the hell away) but I know for sure there will be more than that. A few notes are on the cutouts, which gives them more purpose than a cheap (but extremely cute) jump scare.

Environments

The environments in the game are about what you'd expect after seeing the first room. There's a few environmental obstacles used to slow you down that I've encountered so far, and they did help make me feel slightly more panicked during a monster chase, but beyond the cardboard cut outs that pop up, and a few pools of what I assume were acid placed after a certain level. the environment doesn't offer much danger. A few maze rooms crop up, but you can't walk off the edge, making them more annoying than dangerous. I do like the repeating theme, which illustrates how the game is getting progressively more dark as time goes on efficiently, and without shoving it in your face to get you to notice.

Graphics

Cutesy. That's it. Even as it gets more dark. Cutesy. They did this on purpose.

Story

I'm nowhere near the end, but there's already been a bit of a twist. I know there's a lot more to go before I get to the bottom of it, but from what I've seen, it's intriguing. The story is delivered via notes left by a previous wanderer, and additional notes can be found on random computers in computer rooms. The characters are all interesting, so far. I am attached more to this unnamed unfortunate who explored before me than any other "hey, there's a person who was here before leaving notes" type character. (Does that character have a type name? Because it's starting to seem like the only way story is told in first person horror games.)

Overall

I don't really have a numerical value I can give out for this. I'll just say, I'm not going to keep playing for the gameplay, but I will for the story. That should let you know whether or not you're going to be interested in this game. If you're looking for a good gameplay experience, it's not Spooky's. If you're looking to be entertained immediately, probably also don't bother. If you have some time on your hands, and enjoy story and buildup, you'll probably like it.

The creatures had left as suddenly and mysteriously as they had arrived and though no blood was spilled the tribe of Med'ja-Hom had suffered a terrible wound.

The creatures assault had been the final and greatest blow received by the tribe in recent times and many Med'ja refused to return to the Burrows, choosing instead to remain on the surface taking residence [among the trees.](http://imgur.com/LugVg1C.png) The Burrows they believed, had been cursed by Gods and that to remain there would mean misfortune and death. Those that remained in the tunnels of their home believed that the creatures were a side effect of the Shaman's magic; that the creatures had been attracted by the light of the stones and that they had been little more than an unexpected pest.

One such Med'ja was Char'li who had been working in the lower depths of the Burrows during the assault and had watched as the invaders had carried off the lightstones, ignoring both he and his co-workers who hid among the stones beneath them.

---

In the wake of the exodus trade began as many of the forest dwelling Med'ja still relied on materials that could only be found within their ancestral home. One such material was the salt stone found deep within the Burrows lower levels. In return the Med'ja of the surface provided many of the plant and animal products once collected exclusively by the Hunters and Shamans. The Med'ja-Hom were no longer one tribe but two although a symbiosis between the groups still remained.

Unable to reunite their people the council of Elders decided a new leadership was needed. Lo'te and Ma'te, once Masters of the Hunt and chieftains of War would rule over the Med'ja of the forests as a Duumvirate while Chief Ma'Ten retained his throne as Lord of the Med'ja of the earth with each forming their own council.

---

The Shamans had also felt the effects of the creatures assault with many feeling that their self imposed isolation had made them weak, that the convening of council was not enough to share their knowledge and that they needed to work closer together in order to become strong. So it was that the Cult of Umbralocht sought out a [great tree](http://imgur.com/Fiqr2rp.png) within forest and it was here they made their home, no longer would the Med'ja Shamans live the life of a hermit but together as brothers and scholars
